## How data gets into the book

Nothing in the book reads the pipeline repository directly. Instead:

1. **`data/manifest.yml`** lists every file the book uses from
   [MOT-pipline](https://github.com/CARS-Project/MOT-pipline).
2. **`scripts/sync-pipeline.R`** copies those files into `data/pipeline/`
   (data) and `reports/` (the pipeline's reports, shown as appendices), and
   records the pipeline's commit in `data/pipeline/provenance.csv`.
3. **`scripts/run-examples.R`** runs each query in `sql/` against the vehicle
   table and saves the result in `data/examples/`. The worked examples display
   the same `.sql` files, so the code shown is exactly the code that produced
   the results.
4. **`scripts/run-coverage.R`** counts, for every column of the vehicle table,
   how many vehicles have a value, by year of first use and by year, and saves
   the counts in `data/coverage/` for the coverage sections of the data
   [dictionary](dictionary/index.qmd).
   **`scripts/run-values.R`** likewise summarises each column's values over
   time, in `data/values/`, for the dictionary's Values sections.
5. **Chapters** read the copies with `read_pipeline()` and `read_example()`
   from `R/book.R`, and compute every number, table and chart from them when
   the book is rendered.

The copies are committed, so anyone can rebuild the book without access to the
pipeline or the 9 GB vehicle table.

## Updating after a new pipeline build

From the book's root folder, with MOT-pipline checked out alongside it (or
`MOT_PIPELINE_DIR` set to its location):

```sh
Rscript scripts/sync-pipeline.R   # copy the new outputs
Rscript scripts/run-examples.R    # rerun the examples (needs the parquet)
Rscript scripts/run-coverage.R    # recount column coverage (needs the parquet)
Rscript scripts/run-values.R      # resummarise column values (needs the parquet)
Rscript scripts/rebuild.R         # re-execute every chapter and render
```

Then check the result, and commit `data/`, `reports/` and `_freeze/`. Pushing
to `main` publishes the book.

::: {.callout-important title="Check the words, not just the numbers"}
Numbers in the text are computed, but sentences that interpret them ("the two
averages are almost identical", "most were still tested in Leeds") are
written by hand. After a rebuild, read the chapters whose figures changed and
make sure the text still fits.
:::

If a pipeline file used by the book is renamed or removed, the sync script
stops with an error naming it. Update `data/manifest.yml` and the chapter that
reads it.

## Why `rebuild.R` clears the frozen results

The book uses Quarto's [freeze](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html#freeze)
option: the results of each chapter's code are stored in `_freeze/` and reused
until that chapter's source changes. This is what lets GitHub Actions publish
the book without R. It also means a plain `quarto render` will not pick up new
data, because the chapters themselves have not changed. `scripts/rebuild.R`
deletes `_freeze/` so that every chapter runs again.

## Adding pipeline data to a chapter

1. Add the file to `data/manifest.yml`.
2. Run `Rscript scripts/sync-pipeline.R`.
3. In the chapter, `source("R/book.R")` and read it with
   `read_pipeline("outputs", "tables", ...)`.

To add a worked example, put the query in `sql/` (naming the file as
`'vehicles_enhanced.parquet'`), run `Rscript scripts/run-examples.R exNN`, and
show it with `{{{< include ../sql/exNN_name.sql >}}}` inside a `sql` code
block.

## When the vehicle table gains or loses columns

The data dictionary chapters (`chapters/dictionary/`) each describe a group of
columns, defined once in `dict_groups` in `R/book.R`. A column that has been
removed stops the render with an error naming it. A new column is listed in a
warning on the part's opening page until it is added to a group, and to that
chapter's overview text. Rerun `scripts/run-coverage.R` and
`scripts/run-values.R` after either change. A column whose values should be
charted as categories although it is stored as a number belongs in
`dict_coded`.

## Writing conventions

- Placeholders for material still to come are callouts titled
  **To be written** (or **To be confirmed** for statements to check), with the
  class `.todo`. Search the chapters for `.todo` to list them.
- Pitfalls are callouts titled **Pitfall: ...**, and each is also summarised in
  @sec-pitfalls.
- Charts use `theme_cars()` and the palette in `R/book.R`, with at most four
  series each.

## Publishing

`.github/workflows/publish.yml` renders the book from the frozen results and
publishes it to the `gh-pages` branch on every push to `main`. One-off set-up:
run `quarto publish gh-pages` once locally to create the branch, then in the
repository's settings set GitHub Pages to deploy from the `gh-pages` branch.
The book will then be at
[cars-project.github.io/documentation](https://cars-project.github.io/documentation/).

To preview locally, run `quarto preview`.
